title: Minimax Wasserstein Estimation of Rank-Based Mediation Attribution Laws with Lipschitz Response
banked_reason: D0.5 tier incremental < floor field; salvageable=false; paper_score_ceiling 5 < 7.4. Matched global minimax theorem is sound; the proposed local/adaptive extension requires a new topic.
gap_reasons: making this a narrow endpoint extension below the field floor
Supplied-density equality concerns worst-case rate orders and provides no sharp precision comparison near equal maps, where the target collapses to D0.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matched all-n n^(-1/3) expected-W1 minimax orders for the atom-inclusive attribution law with unknown and supplied mediator densities, including arbitrary randomized probability-valued outputs. Independent audits broadened nuisance assumptions, repaired stale proof closures, and verified five cited foundations; the mathematical referee passed with no findings. D0.5 rated the global contribution incremental below the field floor, and two boundary checks found the proposed local/adaptive extension requires a new topic; the run stopped before F and no Lean proof is claimed.
tldr: The common-rank indirect conditional-mean attribution law has minimax expected Wasserstein-one error of order \(n^{-1/3}\) for every \(n\ge2\), for every control mean \(\mu_0:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) with Lipschitz constant ten. The mediator densities are continuous, nonnegative and normalized on the full closed interval; \(f_0\ge1/2\), and the treated density assigns positive mass to every nonempty interval, while permitting zero density values. The treated outcome regression is arbitrary Borel Bernoulli. The rate requires neither response overlap, pointwise treated density positivity, a density modulus nor a common density upper envelope; supplying the continuous density pair does not improve its order. A total finite histogram and empirical-rank estimator returns a probability measure on \([-1,1]\) with positive normalized weights, including empty counts and atomic null targets. A fixed smooth interior shared-response family yields an exact law isometry and an original Bernoulli converse against every randomized probability-valued procedure. The contribution is a focused incremental endpoint result using credited regression, ordered-transport and Assouad ingredients.
gap: Transport-attribution consistency does not specify the statistical resolution of an entire fitted attribution distribution. Scalar nonsmooth-functional rates and conditional observed-response-law rates do not determine the marginal law of a shared regression evaluated at two prescribed rank arguments.
fill: A single theorem supplies the complete \(n^{-1/3}\) expected-Wasserstein order, a finite positive normalized attainer, and a continuous shared-response law-isometry converse. It gives a prospective precision benchmark for the attribution distributions reported by sequential transport.
